{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-nv-c","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"d51b5e90889b2ac8627066e131b58c578b083c4b6397bb5589ffc6952a603677","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-nv-class-c:lineage:75","source_registry_sha256":"3e184808e042e052d0c78d0dff47c50b34a56560f428649c492afe10bc7ba712","source_liveness_sha256":"0dfbf3aa4b4798b88d69252e076642b5f0a38751c5010711fbce93c8a7d6e292"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Traffic-control confusables and continuation facts","heading":"C2 — Confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: yellow light versus yellow arrows, right versus left on red, stop versus yield, white versus yellow lines, crossing distances, and continuation facts on pre-drive checks, route markers, work zones, pedestrians and trains","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — Confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: yellow light versus yellow arrows, right versus left on red, stop versus yield, white versus yellow lines, crossing distances, and continuation facts on pre-drive checks, route markers, work zones, pedestrians and trains
Confusable pairs among signs, signals and markings, followed by continuation facts that did not fit part C; each block ties to one handbook page, and hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec04-R01 | anchor: A01
Before starting the engine, set the seat for a clear view and easy reach of every control, clean the windshield and windows, buckle up yourself and your passengers, check that you feel calm, and adjust the rear and side mirrors. [A01]
Why it matters: group pre-drive; difficulty low.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-R02 | anchor: A01
Once the engine runs, check the fuel gauge and warning lights, keep the stereo low enough to hear traffic, switch on headlights, signal or wipers if needed, and before moving stop, look and listen for traffic, cyclists and pedestrians. [A01]
Why it matters: group pre-drive; difficulty low.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-R03 | anchor: A02
Both a circle and a crossbuck relate to trains, but the round sign warns that a crossing is ahead while the X-shaped crossbuck marks where the tracks actually are. [A02]
Why it matters: group sign shapes; confusable circle versus crossbuck.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-R04 | anchor: A02
A pentagon is the school-zone and school-crossing shape, whereas a pennant is the no-passing shape. [A02]
Why it matters: group sign shapes; confusable pentagon versus pennant.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-R05 | anchor: A03
A stop sign always requires a full stop, while a yield sign requires slowing and yielding but lets you continue without stopping when the way is clear. [A03]
Why it matters: group signs; confusable stop versus yield.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec04-R06 | anchor: A03
Route signs are usually shields, though shapes and colors differ, and they show US, Interstate and state route numbers. [A03]
Why it matters: group signs; difficulty low.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec04-R07 | anchor: A04
A steady yellow light means stop if you can before entering, a flashing yellow light means go ahead with caution, and a flashing yellow arrow means turn only after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians. [A04]
Why it matters: group signals; confusable three yellow indications.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec04-R08 | anchor: A04
Right on red is allowed after a full stop wherever no sign forbids it, but left on red is allowed only from one one-way street onto another whose traffic flows left. [A04]
Why it matters: group signals; confusable right versus left on red.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec04-R09 | anchor: A04
A flashing red light and a dark, non-working signal both call for a full stop before proceeding, the first treated exactly like a stop sign. [A04]
Why it matters: group signals; confusable flashing red versus signal outage.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec04-R10 | anchor: A04
Cones, drums and barricades steer drivers through work areas and can carry warning lights for night work. [A04]
Why it matters: group work zones; difficulty low.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec04-R11 | anchor: A05
Pedestrians facing a green turn arrow may not cross unless a pedestrian signal or officer allows it, and where a crosswalk is marked they must use it. [A05]
Why it matters: group pedestrians; difficulty medium.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec04-R12 | anchor: A05
Most pedestrian deaths happen mid-block, between intersections, and both drivers and pedestrians share responsibility, so drivers should always be ready to yield. [A05]
Why it matters: group pedestrians; difficulty low.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec04-R13 | anchor: A06
Broken white separates same-direction lanes and allows passing when safe, while solid white between same-direction lanes forbids lane changes and passing. [A06]
Why it matters: group markings; confusable broken versus solid white.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec04-R14 | anchor: A06
White lane lines separate same-direction traffic and white markings also mark road edges, shoulders, crosswalks and stop lines, whereas yellow lines separate opposite-direction traffic [A06].
Why it matters: group markings; confusable white versus yellow.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec04-R15 | anchor: A06
Stop lines are wide white lines across a lane where you stop with a view of traffic from every direction, and dotted white lines either carry a lane line through an intersection or mark freeway exit-only lanes. [A06]
Why it matters: group markings; difficulty medium.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec04-R16 | anchor: A07
Stop at least 15 feet from the tracks when a train comes, but never park within 50 feet of the nearest rail. [A07]
Why it matters: group railroad; confusable fifteen versus fifty feet.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec04-R17 | anchor: A07
At a crossing with more than one set of tracks, wait for a clear view in both directions before starting across, and never shift gears while on the tracks. [A07]
Why it matters: group railroad; difficulty medium.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec04-R18 | anchor: A07
A train cannot stop in time to avoid a car, its speed is hard to judge, and a crossbuck means drivers must yield to trains. [A07]
Why it matters: group railroad; difficulty low.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec04-R19 | anchor: A07
If your vehicle stalls on the tracks, get out at once, find the blue Emergency Notification System sign at the crossing, and notify the railroad and local police. [A07]
Why it matters: group railroad; difficulty medium.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec04-R20 | anchor: A07
School-zone limits are either 15 or 25 mph, and some zones use flashing yellow lights to show when the lower limit is in effect. [A07]
Why it matters: group school zones; confusable two school limits.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0033]
